note_tweet.text:
Our expert @RebeccaLissner traveled to Wisconsin last week as part of CFR's ongoing efforts to understand what Americans think about the United States’ global role. She spent time in two counties, Milwaukee and Kenosha, and met nearly 100 people—from students and farmers to union members and clergy—to discuss everything from tariffs to AI.

“Wisconsin is fed up with tariffs,” Lissner writes. Sentiment toward tariffs was almost universally negative, she reports, with only one business owner noting positive effects of the measures on his steel company. Many people she met across Wisconsin connected the dots between tariffs, increased input costs for companies, and the resultant increase in consumer prices.

“You don’t have to be a rocket scientist to see that the decisions are senseless,” one participant in Kenosha said. Numerous others echoed this, expressing their frustration that those making trade policy do not understand its impact.
